name: Incline dumbbell press
cues: Set the bench to about 30°. Steeper angles shift the work to the front of the shoulders.
Shoulder blades pulled down and back. Head, upper back and hips stay on the bench.
Feet planted on the floor. Don't arch your lower back.
Lower slowly to the sides of your upper chest. No bouncing.
Forearms vertical, elbows under the wrists. Press up until your arms are straight over your shoulders.
safety: No spotter: stop 1–2 reps short. To finish, bring the dumbbells to your chest and sit up with them resting on your thighs.

name: Machine chest press
cues: Set the seat so the handles line up with the middle of your chest.
Back against the pad with its natural curve; don't flatten or arch it. Shoulder blades down and back, and keep them on the pad.
Press until your elbows are straight but not locked. Return slowly.
Don't arch your lower back or let your shoulders roll forward off the pad.
safety: Safe to take close to failure.

name: Machine shoulder press
cues: Set the seat so the handles start level with or a little above your shoulders, elbows slightly in front of your sides.
Back against the pad, abs braced. Don't arch your lower back.
Press until your elbows are nearly straight, not locked. Lower under control to the start.
safety: Safe to take close to failure.

name: Lat pulldown
cues: Lock your thighs under the pad.
Lean back slightly, no more than about 30°, and hold that angle. Don't swing.
Pull the bar to your upper chest.
Drive your elbows down toward your sides. Stop when they stop moving down, then let the bar rise all the way up under control.
safety: Safe to take close to failure.

name: Seated cable row
cues: Feet on the platform, knees slightly bent.
Sit tall, chest up. Keep your back straight the whole set.
Pull the handle to your stomach with your elbows close to your ribs. Pause for a second.
Don't lean back to finish the rep. Straighten your arms slowly on the way back.
safety: Safe to take close to failure.

name: Leg press
cues: Back and tailbone flat on the pad the whole set. Stop lowering before your hips lift or your lower back rounds.
Feet flat on the platform, toes forward, heels down.
Lower until your knees are bent to about 90°. Don't let your thighs press into your ribs. Knees point the same way as your toes.
Push through your whole foot until your legs are straight but not locked.
safety: Never lock your knees at the top. Machine is safe to take close to failure.

name: Bulgarian split squat
cues: Rest the top of your back foot on a bench about knee height.
Stand far enough forward that your front heel stays flat at the bottom.
Lower straight down until your back knee is just off the floor. Don't let it touch.
Hold one dumbbell upright at your chest, elbows in, back straight. Push through your front foot to stand.
safety: One set = all reps on one leg, then the other. Balance is the limit at first: start light and stay 2 reps short of failure.

name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
cues: Feet hip-width, a slight bend in the knees. Keep that same bend the whole rep.
Push your hips straight back to lower the weights.
Back flat and long, chin slightly tucked, eyes on the floor.
Slide the dumbbells down close to your legs. Stop at a strong hamstring stretch (about knee to mid-shin), then drive your hips forward to stand.
safety: If your lower back starts to round, you've gone too low or too heavy. Stay 2 reps short of failure.

name: Seated leg curl
cues: Line your knees up with the machine's pivot. This is the most important setting.
Lower the thigh pad so it holds your thighs snugly.
Set the lower pad on your lower calves, a few inches above your heels. Not on the heel or the Achilles tendon.
Back flat against the pad. Curl as far as you can, then return slowly. No momentum.
safety: Safe to take close to failure.

name: Machine biceps curl
cues: Set the seat so your elbows line up with the machine's pivot, upper arms flat on the pad.
Lower until your arms are nearly straight, under control. Don't let the weight stack touch down.
Curl as far as you can without moving your torso.
safety: Safe to take close to failure.

name: Overhead cable triceps extension
cues: Rope on the low pulley. Face away from the machine with the rope over your head, one foot in front.
Upper arms next to your ears. Elbows stay where they are, the same width apart. Only your forearms move.
Lean slightly forward from the hips, back straight, ribs down. Don't arch your lower back.
Straighten your arms fully without locking, then lower back into the stretch behind your head.
safety: Safe to take close to failure.

name: Dumbbell lateral raise
cues: Keep a slight bend in your elbows. Your elbows lead the way up.
Raise out to the sides until your arms are about shoulder height. No higher. Near the top, keep your thumbs level or slightly up; don't tip your pinkies up.
Shoulders down and back. Don't shrug.
Stand tall with abs braced. No swinging. Lower slowly.
safety: Safe to take close to failure. Good one to do in rest periods.

name: Reverse machine fly
cues: Sit facing the pad with your chest against it. Set it so the handles are at shoulder height.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows the whole time.
Sweep your arms out and back to your sides.
Let the handles come back slowly all the way to the start.
safety: Safe to take close to failure. The pictures are seen from above.

name: Hip adduction machine
cues: Pads against the inside of your knees.
Set the starting width to a comfortable stretch, not a painful one.
Squeeze your legs together, then let them open slowly.
Sit tall with your back on the pad and hold the handles.
safety: Safe to take close to failure.

name: Standing calf raise
cues: Balls of your feet on the edge of the step, heels hanging off.
Lower your heels slowly to a full stretch and pause.
Rise as high as you can and pause at the top.
Knees slightly bent and still. Your ankles do all the moving.
safety: Safe to take close to failure. Good one to do in rest periods.

refs.title: Muscle & Strength: Standing machine calf raise

name: Cable crunch
cues: Rope on the high pulley. Kneel facing it and hold the rope beside your head the whole time.
Crunch by curling your ribs toward your hips, rounding your spine.
Keep your hips still. Don't just bend at the hips or sit back.
Return slowly to the stretch.
safety: Safe to take close to failure. Good one to do in rest periods.
